 Edited by Shubhanshu Dwivedi / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 15, 2026, 07:32 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Mohammed Siraj Mohammed Siraj finally got an opportunity in the series as India brought back the experienced pacer for the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. It is Siraj's first appearance in the series. He last played an ODI against the West Indies in October. "Siraj has been craving an opportunity to play in all formats. He's been around the team for a while and is pretty experienced. He's played over the years, so he knows how to go about things. We're super excited for him as well," India captain Shreyas Iyer said at the toss. Watch Matt Henry on New Zealand’s bowling dominance, India’s batting threats, wobble seam & more New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner won the toss and elected to bowl in the series-deciding match. India lead the five-match series 2-1 after winning the first two games, while the third ODI was washed out. The visitors, however, suffered a 244-run defeat in the fourth match on Friday. India also handed a debut to right-arm seamer Yash Thakur. "He's a jovial guy who has been waiting for the opportunity to play for the country and has been in the scheme of things for a while. I'm glad he's getting the opportunity to prove himself today. It's his debut, so good luck to him," Iyer said. Join conversation
